label: RSI(2) Three-Day Slide (R3)
about: Uptrend stock or ETF whose RSI(2) has fallen three days in a row from below 60 to under 10: a controlled slide rather than one crash day. Buy the next session; sell on a close back above the 5-day average (Connors' R3 rules).

source.title: Connors & Alvarez, Short Term Trading Strategies That Work (2008), the R3 strategy

label: Multiple Days Down
about: Uptrend name that has closed lower four or more sessions in a row. Persistent selling in an uptrend tends to snap back within days (Connors' Multiple Days Down idea, applied to stocks and ETFs).

source.title: Connors & Alvarez, High Probability ETF Trading (2009), Multiple Days Down

label: 200-Day Average Test
about: A stock in a long uptrend (rising 200-day) that was well above its 200-day a week ago pulls back to touch it. Institutions defend that line; buy the test with a limit at the average and target the 20-day average.

source.title: Classic moving-average support test (200-day), e.g. Investopedia: Moving Average (MA) as support

label: Leader 50-Day Average Test
about: Top relative-strength stock above a rising 50-day average dips to touch it with RSI(14) back under 50. Buy the test with a limit at the average; target the 20-day high.

source.title: Moving-average pullback entries in leaders (O'Neil / IBD-style 50-day line tests)

label: Inside Day after a Dip
about: After a short, sharp dip in an uptrend the stock prints an inside day (range inside the prior day's): selling pressure pauses. Buy the next session; target the 7-day closing high, exit on a close above the 5-day average.

label: NR7 Squeeze in a Leader
about: Strong, trending stock prints its narrowest range of the last seven sessions (Crabel's NR7): volatility contraction ahead of expansion. Buy a limit near the close; target the 20-day high.

source.title: Toby Crabel, Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout (1990), NR7

label: Bullish Outside Reversal
about: After a down day in an uptrend, the stock trades below the prior low and then closes above the prior high (a bullish outside / engulfing day). Buy a limit a little below that close; exit on a close above the prior day's high.

label: Low-Volatility Quality Dip
about: Calm, steady large-cap (daily ATR under 2% of price, relative strength at least median) in an uptrend gets a rare RSI(2) washout. Low-volatility names mean-revert most reliably; buy the dip and target the 4-day mean.

source.title: Low-volatility anomaly and short-term reversal in quality stocks (Baker, Bradley & Wurgler, FAJ 2011)

label: High-Volume Capitulation Day
about: Uptrend stock has a heavy-volume down day (2.5x its 20-day volume) that closes near its low with RSI(2) oversold: a selling climax. Buy the next session; exit on a close above the 5-day average.

label: 20-Day VWAP Reclaim
about: Uptrend stock that spent the last sessions below its 20-day volume-weighted price closes back above it: buyers have reclaimed fair value. Buy a limit at the VWAP; target the 20-day high.

source.title: Brian Shannon, Maximum Trading Gains with Anchored VWAP (2023): VWAP reclaims

label: Bollinger Lower-Band Re-entry
about: Uptrend stock or ETF closed below its lower Bollinger band and today closes back inside it on an up day: the classic band re-entry signal. Buy the next session; target the 20-day average.

source.title: John Bollinger, Bollinger on Bollinger Bands (2001): lower-band re-entry

label: RSI(14) Oversold in an Uptrend
about: A stock above a rising 200-day average with 14-day RSI under 30: a rare, deeper washout than the RSI(2) setups catch. Buy the next session and hold up to two weeks for the 20-day average.

source.title: Relative Strength Index oversold readings (Wilder, 1978; Investopedia RSI)

label: ETF Three Down Days in a Calm Bull Market
about: Index or sector ETF above its 200-day falls three sessions in a row while SPY is above its 200-day and VIX is not spiking: a routine pullback in a healthy market. Buy the next session; sell on a close above the prior day's high.

source.title: Connors' consecutive-down-days ETF research (High Probability ETF Trading, 2009)
